build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player places belts on a grid to create paths that carry materials from sources toward machines and output bins. Placed belts visibly connect tiles and define a route. Score 0 if there is no spatial placement, if belts are pre-built with no player agency, or if materials move without any conveyor infrastructure.

Materials visibly move along belts from source toward machines or bins over multiple frames, with smooth or stepped motion that conveys flow. Score 0 if resources teleport, remain static, or are represented only by counters.

At least one machine transforms an input material into a different output product with visible processing feedback such as a progress bar, animation, or state change on the machine sprite. Score 0 if machines are decorative and do not alter item state.

A sorter, splitter, or route-control element visibly sends different item types to different destinations or changes the path based on player configuration. Score 0 if all items follow one fixed path regardless of type or control.

Orders, timers, or deadlines create production pressure: the player must fulfill specific product requests before time expires, and missing a deadline has visible consequences such as lost coins, a warning, or a failed order marker. Score 0 if production has no goals, no time constraint, and no success/failure feedback.

At least three distinct materials or products are present with different icons or colours, and at least two recipe relationships connect them (e.g., ore becomes plate, plate becomes gear). Score 0 if all items are identical or only one material exists.

At least two functionally different machine types are available that accept different inputs or produce different outputs, giving the player a reason to route materials to specific machines. Score 0 if only one machine type exists or all machines behave identically.

An upgrade or planning layer offers at least three choices such as belt speed, machine efficiency, storage capacity, new recipes, or sorter automation, and selecting one visibly changes subsequent play. Score 0 if there is no upgrade or planning system.
Multiple orders or rounds escalate in complexity, requiring longer chains, more products, tighter deadlines, or simultaneous fulfillment. Score 0 if the same single order repeats indefinitely.
A result or summary screen reports fulfilled orders, missed orders, coins earned, and offers retry or title navigation. Score 0 if the game ends abruptly or loops without summary.

Normal startup shows a styled title screen with the game name, a clear Start control, and factory-themed imagery such as belts, machines, crates, or a workshop floor. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI with no theme.

The flow connects title or scenario to factory floor to production play to upgrade or result screen without restarting the executable. Score 0 if a major transition is missing or controls become stuck.

The HUD clearly shows active orders, required products, timer or shift status, produced count, and coins or score in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot tell what to produce or whether the line is working.

Player actions and state changes produce visible feedback: placing a belt shows it on the grid, a machine starting shows processing, an order fulfilled flashes or updates, a jam or failure triggers a warning. Score 0 if changes happen silently with no visual cue.

Art direction is coherent across title, factory floor, belts, machines, items, HUD, upgrades, and result screens with a consistent palette, typography, and iconography. Score 0 if mostly default controls or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Belts, machines, sorters, and material items use real sprite art or carefully composed procedural visuals that read as factory equipment, not plain rectangles or default HTML 引擎 primitives. Score 0 if primary gameplay elements are unstyled ColorRects.

Animation and motion bring the factory to life: belts move or pulse, items travel smoothly, machines show processing cycles, sorters animate their routing, and warnings draw attention with flashes or shakes. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently with no animation.
HUD and UI panels use styled themed widgets with icons, framed panels, or custom fonts rather than raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if all UI is obviously default Label/Button with no theming.
